consumer.use: Decide whether the passed R3 v3 Outcome-Bound admission semantics are feasible on the first three prospective natural Bureau operator-intake identity births without delaying productive work.

decision_target.question: Can exactly three first-in-order post-activation candidate_identity_birth slots be prospectively admitted under C/S/B/E/T/Q with zero binding failures, zero authority violations, zero backfill and median handling <= 10 minutes?

intervention.name: R3-v3 prospective three-slot admission
intervention.description: The experiment is registered as active testing before A while execution_status remains designed. After reviewed merge, set A to one explicit Bureau activation-marker event id; then consume the first three fully provable later candidate identity births in numeric event-id order and attempt C/S/B/E/T/Q binding before productive mutation without delaying work.

control_condition.description: The last three fully provable canonical candidate identity births with event_id < A are frozen after A only as negative eligibility sentinels: each must remain excluded because it predates A. They are not pilot cases and their outcomes are not compared for efficacy.

treatment_condition.description: Exactly the first three fully provable canonical candidate identity births with identity_first_event.event_id > A, subject to the inherited R3 v3 hard birth-proof and self-interference rules.

measurement.method: Before A, bind this experiment in experiments/active.v1.json as state testing with results/decision.yml verdict not_executed and manifest execution_status designed. After exact-head review and merge, create one idempotent Bureau marker whose numeric event id becomes A. For each consumed post-A slot, the terminal-state mapping is fixed: frozen and not_applicable add 0; capture_missed_before_mutation, capture_not_frozen_in_time, result_informed_binding_failure, indeterminate, rejected_interference and rejected_ambiguous_causation each add 1 and immediately REJECT. After canonical birth and ordinal proof, derive deterministic slot_id and, before any C/S/B/E/T/Q analysis, append and exact-readback-verify deterministic slot_claim containing authoritative birth evidence, handling start, UTC start and monotonic_clock_domain. No later ordinal is eligible while any earlier canonical birth has unresolved claim, intent or terminal evidence. After capture analysis, construct the complete terminal record bytes exactly once; freeze terminal_record_bytes_b64 and terminal_record_bytes_sha256 inside deterministic slot_terminal_intent. Before A, freeze a terminal_journal_contract for one already-existing durable controller evidence journal proving caller-keyed create-if-absent records, exact caller-payload readback, authoritative presence/absence, restart durability, provider-returned record_sha256, same-id/same-payload replay and concurrency convergence, and fail-closed same-id/different-payload conflicts; if no existing surface proves those properties, A MUST NOT be written. The terminal record is appended and retried only from the intent-frozen exact byte blob under one deterministic terminal_id. After every success, definite error or ambiguous append, exact-read terminal_id before retry. Matching bytes finish the slot; authoritative absence permits only the same byte-identical same-id retry; unknown presence/absence derives persistence_outcome_unknown and blocks every later ordinal. Persistence transport never changes binding_failure_count, but terminal_identity_conflict immediately REJECTS and any earlier slot still lacking verified claim/intent/terminal evidence at registered review/closeout REJECTS as a material protocol violation.
measurement.success: 3/3 canonical slots, binding_failure_count == 0, zero material review disagreements, zero authority violations, zero replacement/backfill, zero terminal-identity conflicts, median handling_seconds <= 600, at least two definitive non-D0 cases, and no unresolved earlier claim/intent/terminal evidence.
measurement.falsification: Any state with binding_failure_increment=1, experiment interference, ambiguous causation, authority violation, replacement/backfill, noncanonical ordering, post-result binding, material exact-head review disagreement, terminal-identity conflict, or unresolved earlier claim/intent/terminal evidence at registered review/closeout rejects the revision.

cost_metric.method: For every consumed slot, sample handling_started_at_monotonic_ns immediately before the first authoritative candidate-task read in the scan that discovers the candidate or begins its eligibility proof. After canonical birth/ordinal proof, exact-readback-verify slot_claim before any C/S/B/E/T/Q analysis; the claim binds the start timestamp and monotonic_clock_domain. After analysis and failed-capture classification produce a complete provisional terminal payload, sample handling_finished_at_monotonic_ns immediately before persistence. handling_seconds is their monotonic difference divided by 1e9; loss of claim clock-domain continuity forces indeterminate. Construct the exact terminal record bytes once, freeze them as terminal_record_bytes_b64 plus terminal_record_bytes_sha256 inside the verified write-ahead intent, and use only those decoded bytes for every terminal append/retry. Persistence latency is excluded from handling_seconds. A replacement controller must reconcile the same earliest canonical birth and deterministic claim/intent/terminal ids and may never reconstruct a successful binding from later outcome knowledge. PASS requires the three-slot median <= 600 seconds, zero terminal-identity conflicts and no unresolved earlier slot evidence.

comparison.unit: three fixed pre-A negative eligibility sentinels versus three post-A pilot slots
comparability_constraints: activation boundary is the Bureau marker event id A, not a retrospectively selected timestamp
only identity_first_event.event_id ascending determines slot order
no replacement or backfill after any slot outcome
R3 v3 sampling semantics remain unchanged
no Full Outcome Case is collected
confounders: the first three births may contain too few informative non-D0 cases
observer independence may be hard to prove for some slots
three cases establish only tiny-sample feasibility, not product efficacy
